subject: chemistry
intro: Chemistry leads into the laboratories and plants where matter is analysed, transformed and put to work — analytical testing, process design, materials research and forensic science.

roles.title: Chemists
roles.what: Conduct qualitative and quantitative chemical analyses and experiments in laboratories — for quality or process control, or to develop new products and knowledge across industry, medicine and research.
roles.where: Unit 12 is the job description: experimental design, acid-base titrations, chromatography, separation and purification, and identification of ions and gases — all practised from acids-bases-and-ph upward.

roles.title: Materials Scientists
roles.what: Research the structures and chemical properties of metals, alloys, ceramics, semiconductors, polymers and glass, finding ways to strengthen, combine or invent materials with specific properties for new products.
roles.where: Bonding and structure — ionic, covalent, metallic and giant covalent lattices in unit 2 — plus the polymers topics of unit 11 teach exactly the property-structure links this career manipulates.

roles.title: Chemical Engineers
roles.what: Design plant equipment and manufacturing processes for chemicals and products — fuels, plastics, detergents, paper — applying chemistry, physics and engineering principles to production at industrial scale.
roles.where: Stoichiometry and the mole (unit 3), rate of reaction and equilibrium (unit 6), energetics (unit 5) and electrolysis (unit 4) are the calculations behind scaling a reaction from bench to plant.

roles.title: Chemical Technicians
roles.what: Run the chemical and physical laboratory tests that support scientists' analyses of solids, liquids and gases — for research and development, quality control and maintenance of environmental standards.
roles.where: The practical-analysis units — titrations, preparation of salts, chromatography and gas tests from units 7 and 12 — are the bench techniques technicians perform every working day.

roles.title: Forensic Science Technicians
roles.what: Collect, identify, classify and analyse physical evidence from criminal investigations — testing fibres, tissues and substances — and may testify as expert witnesses on evidence and laboratory techniques.
roles.where: Unit 12's identification of ions and gases and chromatography topics are the classic forensic screening tests; the flame tests and precipitation reactions practised here run on crime-lab benches.
